reviews.text: I will edit this review once I finish the game

My secret word was: Cat (I've already provided names in past though I just wanted to share my secret word to get the ball rolling for others to share theirs. But also cause mine was very fitting for me lol) The game is a short read, but nice little horror story. I love that the studio is trying new things with their games. Was a fresh experience. I loved the Soundtrack for the game, and the ambience was really nice. The transitions were smooth. Loved the art for the backgrounds and scenes. I'd say more but I don't want to spoil it for others who have yet to experience it. There was some nice surprises I wasn't expecting. I look forward to future works! In short, I recommend the game to anyone who loves games by this studio, or even if you've never played any by them before. And if you want a little horror game to play during the Halloween Season, or just cause you like horror.

I'm happy to again say, another enjoyable game from Randumb, the experience was different from their previous titles I've played which I liked! I also really appreciated the decision to go for a free to play for this game. I enjoyed the art styling, the music and the story that was presented. As always, keep safe everyone and enjoy the little things that can bring joy (like this game) and of course Secret Word: HORROR

Special Word: Cat It' a short, sweet little story with a little bit of game play sprinkled in. Honestly, it was enjoyable except with a slight hiccup with a character stuck on a phrase without the text advancing no matter what I did. Had to restart from an older save once I shut the game down.

Secret word: Vengeance I am... honestly conficted about the use of AI art/music, just the fact of it, and also the... uh... *player interaction*, using the entire community to come up with names for your characters. Its certainly unusual, and it makes me wary of implications. But damn me if i'm not excited to see my name pop up in one these games! P.S.: reading more of the reviews i lowkey have to agree that it felt like the whole thing was AI generated in some way shape form, from art and music to even the story and dialogue perhaps?? That's not a good thing, do not stoop down to that level.

Wish I could mark this review as Mixed, cause this game has some good in it, but I can't help but feel like this is a very bad omen for this studio's future. But first, the good: -The character dialogue was actually pretty good and funny. Especially with the barmaid unexpectedly being based. I know others have complained about it being too raunchy and lacking subtlety, but to me it felt perfect for most of the characters, although I think it got a bit excessive with Art. -The story felt more concise and coherent than a lot of their other titles I've played. -Letting players name characters is actually really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. -It's a free game, so the complaints I'm about to levy aren't quite as severe as if this were a game I'd paid for. Now the bad: -The use of generative AI got kind of obnoxious. It's a free game, and they claim to not be using models based off assets they don't own, so I'm not going to touch on the ethical/legal side here for the art specifically, just how it affects the game: It makes the whole game's style very inconsistent. Certain parts like the character sprites are obviously cleaned up thoroughly in post and look decent, but a lot of the CG's had little to no work done at all, and have a lot of generation artifacts. The dialogue, at least, was completely human written. I can tell that much. However, there's also what I suspect to be ai-generated music in this game. It's possible I'm mistaken, but if it is, then I'm concerned they just dumped some prompts into Suno and called it a day. That's not ethical in any light, and it's especially scummy to then sell those tracks as an "Original Soundtrack" for ten whole dollars here too. Hope I'm wrong, cause otherwise I don't feel comfortable supporting these developers any further. -The story, despite being more clear and concise, was pretty bland. Just "Bad guy gets caught by psycho who tortures and kills him as revenge for something he did. Oh and there's a weird doll too." Which could be good, but wasn't well executed. The whole thing felt like it didn't really have a point, and if the intent was just to make a short, spooky experience then, sorry, but it just didn't really work that well. It's maybe a good launchpad for making games that are less choice-heavy, but still. -There's just not really much of the charm from their older titles present here, in every way. Despite everything, my secret word was Cat, and I hope the issues with this game don't become a trend.

Secret word: Story After experiencing The Test, I was excited for this new title from the same devs. The whole idea of using player-chosen names is great, and for me it's the main attraction. I appreciate the effort the devs made to keep the game free. However, free as it might be, there are issues with this game. As a dev myself, I know just how important feedback is, and I've taken the time to discuss these issues so the devs can improve their future games. My main concerns are about UX, balancing, art/music, and the story. These concerns are my own, and if they don't resonate with you then that's fine. [UX] As others mentioned, there are text 'hiccups'. Moments where a dialog phrase or line ends, and there is a pause before the next one. This pause can't be skipped with the Enter key. I suspect these pauses are there for emphasis, and to help induce a specific intonation (but I could be wrong). However, they should be skippable. Pressing the Enter key should allow you to skip this wait time, and start the next phrase/line. Some people like to read a little faster, and so slowing the dialog down can make the experience a little worse. Since these pauses repeat over and over again, it turns from mildly annoying to infuriating. Now, what's really the issue with the dialog being slow? Well, it's because of the story. Dialog is often predictable, and so the player may want to only skim through some dialog and get to the interesting, mysterious bits. Pressing Enter just to see that it doesn't work is annoying. Don't force pauses unless you have a very good reason to do so. I will quote the documentation of a popular visual novel engine (Ren'Py): "In general, using hard pauses is rude. When the user clicks to advance the game, it's an explicit request. [b] To override that request is to assume you understand what the player wants more than the player does [/b]". [Balancing] Specific aspects of the game are neglected, mostly the story. The art and music are fine, but they feel overengineered. As good as they might be, the story drags them down and bottlenecks their potential. There are many good games with very bland or even "bad" art (see Higurashi). However, these games are often highly praised for their very good story and character development. They are still good games. Therefore, the takeaway here is to spend more time on the core aspects of the game, and less on the fluff. Art is nice, but many people might come for the core game itself: the story and secret word system. Try to see how you can take advantage of that. If you want to keep the art and soundtrack, then spend more time on the story to bring it up to a similar level. If you want to present your work as an art more than a game, putting emphasis on the art and soundtrack, then that's fine, but you should also mention that in the description. This helps players to create adequate expectations. [Music/Art] Others seem to have a problem with AI-generated content. I believe that AI content is only bad when you notice it, or when it's the only thing holding the game together. In this game, both the music and art feel AI generated. And no, it's not about being nit-picky with the details. I'm talking about seeing the art and instantly thinking it was AI generated. There's a specific style it has. The soundtrack felt a bit...odd. It didn't seem to fit the game entirely. However, if the other aspects of the game were good, then it wouldn't be an issue. Unfortunately, the story is disappointing, and so all the effort put into these assets could've be put somewhere else. See the previous Balancing section. Also, find a way to integrate the music with the story moments, so that they go hand-in-hand. [Story] First off, I'm not sure if the secret word corresponds to a significantly altered story path. My word was "Story" and I tried to explore the map a decent amount before moving on to the main objectives. I'll therefore base my review on this specific path, and I'll try not to spoil anything. At first, I was intrigued, not knowing where the story will lead. However, after a bit, a lot of stuff became very predictable. So much so that I was waiting for the good mystery to come. Before I could find such a moment, the credits started rolling. The characters felt generic and shallow. Some of them, like the Bard, I feel lacked purpose. Sure, it's great for world building. But remember: the Bard appears only briefly, and has its own art. Time was spent on that art, time which could've gone into the development of the story. There is very little time for tension to build. The fact that the events are predictable doesn't help at all. There are some elements with unanswered questions. This is good; leaving players with some questions lets them speculate, and in the end will leave them wanting to experience more from the same universe/franchise. However, the story feels so generic that it doesn't create that feeling in the end.

I usually really enjoy your games, but the AI in this one is way too present for my taste. I know the game is free, and you said it wasn't stolen art, but that doesn't take away the fact that AI art just doesn't have any soul and fairly looks awful on some illustrations; the music in particular is just painful to hear. Hope you'll stop using that even if it slows you down :/ Also, I hear you when you say you used AI for a minority of the content, but when that content is either used a lot (music) or supposed to have a big impact (special illustration like the eye, the doll, the puppy, etc...), it does feel like the majority of the game is AI-generated. Sure, you didn't use AI for every RPGmaker tile, but that doesn't take away the overall impact of the AI "art" on your game.
Secret word: Story Short but it's good to have little break of full gaming grind to relax and see how the story goes. Plus it's FREE! and the music song in end is awesome.

I already have been picked, but I wanted to share what my word was anyway: Special Word: Kitten. Now that that is out of the way, I really liked this game. I played it on stream and we all got to enjoy the beautiful art, the FANTASTIC soundtrack, and the lovely story with its strange little ins and outs and subtexts. The characters were fantastic and while it was a psychological horror, we had quite a few good laughs for Comedy and Horror are one in the same. Thank you for making this game, devs. I can't wait to see what comes in the future.

Once again, Randumb studios does not disappoint! The music is amazing, the ambiance is creepy, the dialogue is funny! They really hit all of the marks! The end is glorious, the art is fantastic! I would play it over and over again! It's always exciting when they release a new game because you just know it will be great every time, and I have never been let down! Keep up the amazing work! I know I have already been picked, but my word is: KITTEN <3

Secret code was...: secret (surprising enough lol) Honestly, I was expecting to see some delicious cringe artsy stuff, but this game was deliciously delightful and devilishly fiendish at times. I had a lot of fun reading the voices in character. And not to mention that banger soundtrack, bit on the nose but it was too good to not want to sing to lol I really liked this games personality. Maybe I should take it out to dinner :3
A perfect short story for the season

I'm pleasantly in awe how much work went into this short horror game and it's all for free. I was met with an incredible rock ballad the moment I opened the game. The story line was wonderfully paced and the gore was... a work of art. It was a much needed distraction from the election blues I was feeling and I appreciate the heartfelt messages at the credits. You have a fan for life. I received RITUAL for my keyword.

A thief needed fiscal salvation so he robbed an old man on vacation. [spoiler]But it was all a fake Art, in fury, said "Snake!" "Your blood will give such inspiration!"[/spoiler] [spoiler]My secret word was "cat".[/spoiler]

This is truly a work of Art. Short and sweet. The ending music doesn't fit the atmosphere though. I'd prefer the intro scene's BGM instead. Also, my secret word is [b]garden[/b] Which sounds fitting since I love the garden the most.
My special word was Happy, which is fabulous for an atmospheric horror such as this one <3

Short and sweet. Quite an impactful story. Really neat pieces of artwork. A fair bit of curious questions unanswered, I have to admit, however... perhaps that's part of the charm? Or for future plans? Also, GREAT soundtrack! I've played all the Test games and loved them. Always interested in your works. You do indeed seem very passionate about them. That's always a big plus regarding game creators. Personal word: Puppy
一款恐怖风的视觉小说，美术风格独特，好像是哥特风？黑暗而华丽，音乐带感，渲染得氛围很好，角色塑造得也不错，虽然小姐姐们出场的机会很少是了。 由于不是母语，剧情看的磕磕绊绊的，但是大概了解是什么故事了，真是猜错主角系列，[spoiler] art真是微笑的艺术疯子，为了艺术去狩猎，但兄弟俩也不是好人，恶人自有恶人磨。 [/spoiler] 作为免费游戏，质量还算可以，推荐。
Word is Tavern. Game is incredibly short. The game isn't a questionnaire either. I'm giving this one a No, though it feels mixed to me.

Special Word: Magic This title was really nice for a free game, I wish it was longer as I wanted to know more about the characters and why some of them acted so strangely. All in all it was a fun and intriguing little experience. :D
